title: Installing PySpark on Mac with pipenv
question:
I have a setup where I use pipenv for my virtual environments. I am using a MacBook.

I have done the following:

  • Installed openJDK 11 using brew
  • Set paths in the .zprofile folder:
eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
export JAVA_HOME="/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@11"
export PYSPARK_PYTHON="/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.10/bin/python3.10"
export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/python@3.10/bin:$PATH"
  • Install pipenv using pip.
  • Install all dependencies using pipenv install -e ., here pyspark version 3.3.0 is included.
  • Activate the shell pipenv shell
  • I use VS code, when I run all tests they pass as expected.

However, when I then run pyspark in the terminal in the activated shell environment, I get an error:

/Users/<user_name>/.local/share/virtualenvs/<repo_name>/bin/pyspark: line 24: /bin/load-spark-env.sh: No such file or directory
/Users/<user_name>/.local/share/virtualenvs/<repo_name>/bin/pyspark: line 68: /bin/spark-submit: No such file or directory
/Users/<user_name>/.local/share/virtualenvs/<repo_name>/bin/pyspark: line 68: exec: /bin/spark-submit: cannot execute: No such file or directory

When I follow the path /Users/<user_name>/.local/share/virtualenvs/<repo_name>/bin/pyspark there is no folder pyspark but in the path /Users/<user_name>/.local/share/virtualenvs/<repo_name>/bin/ the files (load-spark-env.sh and spark-submit) which causes errors are located. What am I doing wrong here?
answer:
My first guess would be that SPARK_HOME is not set in that shell.

Usually I'm forced to set one or more of following 5 variables depending on where (Windows, Linux, Mac) and how (spark-shell/pyspark/IDE/...) I'm running a spark locally.

Here is for my current Windows setup (obviously you'll have to use export ... instead of set ...):

set SPARK_HOME=C:\My\workspaces\project\.venv\Lib\site-packages\pyspark\
set HADOOP_HOME=C:\My\workspaces\project\.venv\Lib\site-packages\pyspark\
set JAVA_HOME="C:\ProgFiles\jdk-1.8"
set PYSPARK_DRIVER_PYTHON=C:\My\workspaces\project\.venv\Scripts\python3
set PYSPARK_PYTHON=C:\My\workspaces\project\.venv\Scripts\python3

I would start with first 3, then set last 2 if it doesn't work.

If setting these 5 doesn't work and you need to debug further then I would start adding set -x to each script in the chain of execution starting with pyspark. I.e. change /Users/<user_name>/.local/share/virtualenvs/<repo_name>/bin/pyspark from

#!/usr/bin/env bash

#
# Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one or more
# contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file distributed with

to

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -x

#
# Licensed to the Apache Software Foundation (ASF) under one or more
# contributor license agreements.  See the NOTICE file distributed with
